title: Tokyo · Osaka · Kyoto · Nagoya · Tokyo: A 15-day multi-city adventure through Japan's cultural heartland — tailored for car lovers on their first trip
description: From the neon-drenched streets of Shibuya to the legendary Toyota factories of Nagoya, this itinerary weaves Japan's deep car culture with ancient temples, street food obsessions, and family-friendly experiences across five cities.

activities.name: Land at Haneda & Check In
activities.description: Clear customs, grab Suica/PASMO cards, take Keikyu Line to hotel. Walk the world's busiest intersection. Stand at Mag's Park rooftop (free!) for the view, find Hachiko statue.

activities.name: Shibuya Sky
activities.description: 46th floor open-air rooftop for 360-degree sunset views of Tokyo.
tips: Jet lag strategy: push through to 9pm. Eat well, hot bath, and your body clock adjusts faster.

activities.name: MEGA WEB / Gazoo Racing Garage
activities.description: Toyota's mega showroom in Odaiba. Latest models, racing cars, concept vehicles. The History Garage has classic 2000GTs, AE86s, and vintage JDM legends. Kids can drive on the mini course.
details: Free entry, Yurikamome Line to Aomi

activities.name: teamLab Borderless
activities.description: Immersive digital art at Azabudai Hills. Flowing art, infinity mirrors, interactive light rooms. Allow 2-3 hours.
details: Book well in advance — sells out during Golden Week

activities.name: Daikoku PA Car Meet
activities.description: THE pilgrimage for car lovers. Taxi to Daikoku PA — the legendary highway rest stop where JDM culture comes alive after dark. Skyline GT-Rs, Supras, drift cars, bosozoku bikes. Free, chaotic, unforgettable.
details: Peak: 10pm-1am, best on dry weekend nights

activities.name: Senso-ji Temple
activities.description: Arrive before 9am. Walk through the Thunder Gate, browse Nakamise-dori, draw a fortune slip (omikuji).

activities.name: Akihabara Electric Town
activities.description: Multi-floor arcades, electronics, gashapon alleys. For car fans: die-cast models and 1:24 JDM kits at Tamiya and Mandarake. 450m observation deck — incredible views if weather is clear.
details: Hunt for AE86 and GT-R model kits

activities.name: Meiji Shrine
activities.description: Walk through towering torii gates into forested grounds. Write a wish on an ema plaque. Rainbow chaos — crepe stands, wild fashion, candy shops.

activities.name: Shinjuku Gyoen
activities.description: Beautiful gardens with late April wisteria and azalea blooms. Pack a konbini bento for a garden picnic.
tips: Golden Week tip: Shinjuku Gyoen closes at capacity. Arrive before noon.

activities.name: Kabukicho & Golden Gai
activities.description: Shinjuku's neon entertainment district then maze of 200+ tiny bars.

activities.name: Shinkansen to Osaka
activities.description: Hikari Shinkansen from Tokyo Station, about 2h40m at 285 km/h. Sit on the right (E-seat) for Mt. Fuji views around 40 min in.

activities.name: Shinsekai District
activities.description: Retro entertainment district with neon, arcades, 1960s vibe. Tsutenkaku Tower for panoramic views.
tips: Osaka people are louder, funnier, warmer. Ask 'osusume wa?' (what do you recommend?) and watch them light up.

activities.name: Dotonbori Night Walk
activities.description: Neon strip along the canal — Glico Running Man, giant crabs, endless takoyaki. Walk the south bank, eat everything.

activities.name: Kuromon Market Breakfast
activities.description: Fresh sashimi, grilled scallops, wagyu skewers, tamagoyaki, tropical fruit. Come hungry, go before 10am. Cross stone bridge, climb to 8th floor for panoramic views. Late April: possible late cherry blossoms.

activities.name: Amerikamura
activities.description: Vintage clothing, street art, record shops. Triangle Park is the hangout.

activities.name: Umeda Sky Building Sunset
activities.description: Floating Garden Observatory for sunset over Osaka.

activities.name: Universal Studios Japan
activities.description: Full-day adventure. Priorities: Super Nintendo World (timed entry via app), Wizarding World of Harry Potter, Mario Kart ride. Arrive 30 min before gates.
details: Express Pass worth it during Golden Week
Strategy: Nintendo first, Harry Potter, then others

activities.name: Train to Kyoto
activities.description: JR Special Rapid from Osaka to Kyoto (about 30 min, JR Pass). Arrive before 8am — towering bamboo with almost no crowds. Light filtering through is otherworldly.

activities.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
activities.description: Gold-leafed pavilion reflected in its mirror pond. Looks photoshopped — in person it's surreal.

activities.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine
activities.description: Thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up Mt. Inari. Full hike 2-3 hours, but even 30 min gives incredible photos.
details: Free, open 24 hours, JR Inari Station
tips: Walk past the first 200m where everyone stops. After Yotsutsuji intersection (30 min up), paths are nearly empty.

activities.name: Gion District
activities.description: Stroll the geisha district as lanterns light up. Hanami-koji is most photogenic.

activities.name: Shinkansen to Nagoya
activities.description: Hikari from Shin-Osaka to Nagoya — just 50 minutes. Welcome to the automotive capital of Japan.

activities.name: Explore Sakae
activities.description: Nagoya's main entertainment district. Oasis 21 is a stunning futuristic structure with a glass 'spaceship' hovering above a park.
tips: Nagoya is Japan's most underrated food city. Its own cuisine: miso katsu, hitsumabushi (eel), tebasaki (wings), kishimen (flat noodles).

activities.name: Sakae Nightlife
activities.description: Nagoya nightlife around Sakae and Nishiki. More relaxed than Tokyo — local izakayas are welcoming and cheaper.

activities.name: Toyota Automobile Museum 🏎️
activities.description: THE car lover's dream. 140+ vehicles tracing automobile history from the 1890s to today — European classics, American muscle, and Japanese legends including Skylines, Supras, Celicas, and Fairlady Zs. The special 'What's JDM?' exhibition covers Japan's rad era cars and runs through April 2026. Allow 2-3 hours.
details: 🚗 The JDM exhibit alone is worth the trip to Nagoya

activities.name: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry & Technology
activities.description: Back in central Nagoya, this museum tells Toyota's story from textile looms to the global auto giant. The Automobile Pavilion has robot demos, engine cutaways, and a production line simulation. Kids love the hands-on Technoland zone. Nagoya's landmark with its golden shachihoko (fish-tiger) roof ornaments. The Honmaru Palace restoration is stunning — intricate painted fusuma panels in every room.
tips: Hitsumabushi hack: eat the first portion plain, the second with green onion and wasabi, the third as tea broth. Then the fourth however you liked best. That's the official way.

activities.name: Shinkansen to Tokyo 🚅
activities.description: Hikari from Nagoya to Tokyo — 1 hour 40 minutes. Your last bullet train of the trip. Enjoy the scenery.

activities.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
activities.description: The inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market is still a food paradise. Stall after stall of grilled seafood, fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and matcha treats. Eat your way through. Nissan's sleek showroom in the heart of Ginza. See the latest GT-R, Z cars, and concept vehicles. Free entry, air-conditioned, and the design is beautiful.

activities.name: Ginza Evening Stroll
activities.description: Japan's most upscale shopping district glows at night. Window-shop designer flagships, pop into the multi-floor Uniqlo for souvenirs, and enjoy the clean, elegant energy.

activities.name: Toyosu Fish Market
activities.description: Wake up early for the world's largest fish market. Watch the famous tuna auction from the observation deck (lottery required for floor access). The market floor is visible through glass windows. Then eat the freshest sushi of your life at the market restaurants.

activities.name: Yokohama — Nissan Global HQ Gallery
activities.description: Train to Yokohama (~30 min from Tokyo). Nissan's global headquarters has a free showroom with GT-R heritage cars, NISMO editions, and concept vehicles. For car fans, this is a must. Japan's largest and oldest Chinatown. Grab nikuman (steamed buns), stir-fried noodles, and wander the ornate gates. A nice change of pace from Japanese food.

activities.name: Osanbashi Pier Sunset
activities.description: Walk the wooden whale-back pier for panoramic Bay Bridge and skyline views. Beautiful at sunset.

activities.name: Train to Hakone
activities.description: Romancecar express from Shinjuku to Hakone-Yumoto (~85 min, scenic route). Buy the Hakone Free Pass for unlimited transport on buses, boats, cable cars, and trains within Hakone for 2 days. Stunning outdoor sculpture garden set against the Hakone mountains. Picasso pavilion, giant installations, and a stained-glass tower you can walk through. Beautiful for all ages.

activities.name: Owakudani Volcanic Valley
activities.description: Take the Hakone Ropeway over sulfurous volcanic vents. At the top, eat a kuro-tamago (black egg) boiled in the hot springs — legend says each adds 7 years to your life. Hop on one of the colorful 'pirate ships' for a cruise across Lake Ashi. On clear days, Mt. Fuji towers over the lake — one of the most iconic views in Japan.
details: 🥚 Black eggs: ¥500 for 5 — you'll eat them all
🗻 Clear mornings have the best Fuji views

activities.name: Hakone-Yumoto Onsen
activities.description: End the day soaking in a hot spring (onsen) in Hakone-Yumoto town. Many ryokan offer day-use onsen for visitors. Tenzan and Hakone Yuryo are popular choices with outdoor rock baths.
details: 📝 Onsen etiquette: wash before entering, no swimwear, small towel on head
tips: If anyone has tattoos: many onsen ban them. Look for 'tattoo-friendly' signs or book a private (kashikiri) bath. Hakone Yuryo has private options.

activities.name: Choose Your Adventure
activities.description: Your last full day — tailor it to what you loved most. Options: Shimokitazawa for vintage shopping and coffee, Ikebukuro for Pokémon Center and Sunshine City, or revisit a favorite neighborhood for deeper exploration. Hunt for car souvenirs: Tomica die-cast cars (¥500 each, available at toy stores and convenience stores), JDM model kits at Yellow Submarine (Akihabara), or automotive magazines at any large bookstore.
details: 🛍️ Shimokitazawa: bohemian village vibe, best vintage in Tokyo
🎮 Ikebukuro Sunshine City: Pokémon Center, J-World, aquarium
🚗 Tomica makes miniatures of nearly every JDM car ever — perfect gifts

activities.name: Don Quijote Souvenir Run
activities.description: The legendary discount megastore has EVERYTHING. Kitkat flavors (matcha, sake, strawberry cheesecake), Japanese snacks, beauty products, electronics, and weird gadgets. The Shibuya location is open 24 hours.
details: 💡 Tax-free purchases over ¥5,000 — bring your passport

activities.name: Farewell Tokyo Dinner
activities.description: Make your last night special. Options range from a splurge yakiniku dinner to a casual izakaya crawl. Whatever you choose, raise a glass of Asahi or highball to an unforgettable 2 weeks in Japan.
tips: Last night shopping tip: Don Quijote and most konbini are open 24 hours. No rush on souvenirs — you can grab them at midnight if needed.

activities.name: Last Morning in Japan
activities.description: Sleep in or take one final walk around your neighborhood. Visit a nearby konbini for last-minute Kit Kat flavors and onigiri for the road. Check out and head to the airport. Japanese airports have incredible shopping. Haneda and Narita both have duty-free sections with regional sweets, sake, and last-chance souvenirs. The royce chocolate and Tokyo Banana are classic picks.
details: ✈️ Narita: 60–90 min via Narita Express (¥3,070) or Skyliner (¥2,520)
🛒 Get there 2–3 hours early for international — the shopping alone takes an hour
tips: Return your IC card (Suica/PASMO) at any JR ticket counter for your ¥500 deposit back. Or keep it as a souvenir — it works forever and you'll need it when you come back. And you will come back.
